title: Standing of City-paid charities with the Attorney General's registry
question: Which City-paid charities does the State registry show as delinquent, past due, revoked or expired, and is the City still paying them?
finding: Of 15 charities checked on 20 November 2026, 6 are delinquent or revoked and 2 more registered but past due. Still paid in fiscal 2026 or 2027 while past due: Chinese Progressive Association $956,433; Mid Market Foundation $3.6 million. The delinquent ones (Oakes Children's Center, last paid FY2023, San Francisco Safe, last paid FY2024, GlobalSF, last paid FY2023, Hearing and Speech Center of Northern California, last paid FY2023, Southeast Consortium for Equitable Partnerships, last paid FY2023) are no longer paid under their own names. United Council of Human Services was revoked on 09/18/2023 after more than a year suspended (letter in charity-filing-facts); the City paid for its programs through fiscal sponsors.
how: Status lines are those the owner recorded from the registry's verification portal (the “REGISTRY STATUS” text). City payments are summed by fiscal year for the organization's payee name; Felton Institute is counted for San Francisco Suicide Prevention, which merged into it.
limits: "Past due" or "Due" can mean only that the latest renewal has not been processed; the registry often lags filings by months. A delinquent charity may not solicit or disburse charitable funds, but the City pays for services under contract, and the registry status is not a City contracting rule. Payments through fiscal sponsors are not counted under the charity's own name.
